# Run ledger — P26.6 (agenda content depth: index records → typed claims)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.6__agenda-content-claims.md` (SOURCES.6).
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-6-agenda-content-claims` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-5-vendor-tenant-universe` (tip `90157ba`, PR #97).
- **Date:** 2026-09-17. Engineering under GL-GATE-06 + ADR-087; every host's
  robots decides, never bypassed. Code commits `99aa596` (implementation),

## What landed

### 1. Bounded document continuation (`discover_more`)

Each agenda-platform **index** capture is now the discovery surface for its
linked agenda/minutes/matter documents — one bounded, network-isolated pass
(P25.5's `Connector.discover_more` seam):

- **Legistar** — `{api_base}/matters/{MatterId}` (the documented InSite matter
  detail; `doc_required_fields=["MatterId"]`).
- **PrimeGov** — the meeting's own `itemsSearchResultsDefaultLinkOnMeetingPortal`
  field names the portal document (`doc_link_keys` — the URL comes from the
  captured payload, never constructed).
- **CivicClerk** — `/v1/Meetings/{agendaId}` for events whose `agendaId` is
  non-zero (`doc_required_fields=["id"]`).
- **eScribe** — `{api_base}/Meeting.aspx?Id={ID}` (the server-rendered public
  agenda page).

**Reviewed window bounds ride the target row as data** — `doc_per_tenant`
(most-relevant items first: vocabulary-/contract-type tier-0, then canonical
recency order) and `doc_run_cap` (per-platform run ceiling)
come from the `[platform_endpoints.*]` rows in `procurement_vocab.toml`
(vocab `2026.09.17-p26.6`) and are copied onto every `tenant_targets()` row —
a test pins that shrinking the row's bound shrinks the fan-out.

**Canonical window order (`doc_order_fields`).** The bounded selection ranks
items by the reviewed per-platform date field — most recent first (Legistar
`MatterLastModifiedUtc`, CivicClerk `startDateTime`, PrimeGov `meetingDate`,
eScribe `StartDate`), item id as tie-break — item DATA, never the server's
return order. This is load-bearing: eScribe's `GetCalendarMeetings` returns the
same meeting set in a **different order per call** (verified live 2026-09-17 —
two fetches 45s apart, same 474-meeting set, 465/474 positions shuffled), so a
position-based window slides between re-runs while a canonical one is a
function of the item *set*.

| platform | doc_per_tenant | doc_run_cap | doc genre |
|---|---|---|---|
| legistar | 20 | 350 | json (+pdf sniff) |
| primegov | 20 | 100 | any (payload link → sniff) |
| civicclerk | 20 | 350 | json (+pdf sniff) |
| escribe | 20 | 300 | html (+pdf sniff) |

### 2. The reviewed agenda-content vocabulary

`connectors/src/connectors/data/agenda_content_vocab.toml` (vocab
`2026.09.17`) — 15 reviewed `[[terms]]` covering the ticket's surveillance
domain (alpr, flock_safety, vigilant, rtcc, drone/uas, shotspotter/
soundthinking, surveillance_ordinance/ccops, facial_recognition,
body_worn_camera, cctv, cell_site_simulator, predictive_policing,
gunshot_detection, social_media_monitoring) **plus** `contract_notice`
mirroring the reviewed `contract_matter_patterns` family. Patterns carry
word-boundary anchors where a bare substring would false-positive
(`\buas\b`, `\balpr\b`). The table also carries the Part VIII
`forbidden_tokens`/`person_naming_predicates` guards applied to every emitted
literal — a literal carrying a per-datum token is suppressed and recorded on
the document row, never emitted.

### 3. Verbatim claims with document locators

A captured document parses by its declared genre through the P07.1 helpers
(`pdf_text_pages` / `html_text` / `utf8_text`) — captured bytes only. Each
matched term emits a `content_term` claim on the matter's `agenda_item` subject
(and additionally on the `contract:` subject when the item's type matches
`contract_matter_patterns`):

- `value` = the term id; `raw_value` = the **verbatim literal slice** of the
  captured text (OKC convention — never normalized, never inferred);
- `evidence.locator` = `byte_range` into the extracted document text, or a
  1-based `page` locator for PDFs;
- **no per-capture id inside the claim** — `capture_digest` deliberately does
  NOT ride the claim's evidence dict, because it keys the claim's
  `content_digest` and a byte-volatile page (eScribe `Meeting.aspx` embeds
  churning CSRF/viewstate bytes — 326/368 captures differed on an identical-
  content re-run) would mint a new claim per fetch. The capture↔document map
  stays durable on the `agenda_document` row and in the fetch record's
  `document_outcomes` (the OKC convention carries no capture id either).

Each document also emits an `agenda_document` run row (outcome
`matched`/`no_match`/`empty`, capture digest, byte size, matched term ids, the
window bounds it resolved under) plus a `document` claim naming the fetched
document URL on the item subject.

### 4. Fail-closed per document

- A child document that doesn't parse as the platform's declared genre —
  non-JSON where JSON was declared, an InSite error envelope, a JSON object
  missing every `doc_required_fields` key, or an unreviewed media type —
  raises `ContentDrift`. The pipeline records it per-document on
  `report.drifted` (id/url/platform/tenant/document_kind/detail) and the run
  continues; drift on a *seed* capture still propagates and fails the run.
- A robots-refused child fetch lands on `report.refusals`; a 404/gone
  document lands on `report.disappearances`; an empty capture records
  `outcome="empty"`. Nothing is fabricated.
- `runner.py` `FetchRecord.document_drift` + `SourceRunReport.drifted` carry
  the per-document dispositions into the fetch record / GCS run row;
  `ops.scheduled` surfaces the count in the run-row `detail`.

### 5. Fixtures + tests

`tests/connectors/test_agenda_documents.py` — 23 tests over new fixtures
(`legistar_seattle_matter_11400.json`, `civicclerk_maui_events.json`,
`civicclerk_maui_meeting_4501.json`, `escribe_nanaimo_meeting.html`,
`primegov_portal_meeting.html`, `agenda_cctv_doc.pdf`) covering: bounds-as-data,
all four platforms' document paths, PDF page locators, verbatim `raw_value`
verified against captured text at the locator range, genre drift recorded
per-document while the run continues, missing-required-fields drift, empty
outcome, robots-refused → recorded refusal, 404 → recorded disappearance,
bounded window (`doc_per_tenant` honoured), set-stable window selection under
shuffled index order (unit + end-to-end), rerun idempotency, and the
Part VIII guards. `make check` green (ruff/format/mypy/pytest/verify-gen).

Cloud SQL proxy `127.0.0.1:5433` → `sig-pg`; password via
`gcloud secrets versions access sig-pg-password` → env only.

| measure | before (P26.6 first run) | after (final state) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claim` rows | 24,732 | 32,064 | +7,332 |
| `predicate_id='content_term'` | 0 | 612 | +612 (new predicate) |
| `predicate_id='document'` | 1,126 | 3,979 | +2,853 |

`content_term` breakdown after: contract_notice ~580, cctv ~8, rtcc 4,
vigilant 3, drone 3, body_worn_camera 2, surveillance_ordinance 2, alpr 1
(the contract-family term dominates by design — reviewed vocab, per-term
selectivity is a vocabulary concern, not a code one). `agenda_item:*`
subjects: 1,000+.

**Idempotent re-run — the honest sequence (two real defects found and fixed):**

1. Pre-fix re-run `sig-ingest-escribe` (run row `16-34-13`): **+328 rows** —
   eScribe `Meeting.aspx` is byte-volatile (CSRF/viewstate churn;
   326/368 capture digests differed) and `evidence.capture_digest` keyed the
   claim's `content_digest` → duplicate claims on identical content.
   **Fix:** capture_digest leaves the claim evidence dict (the OKC
   convention); it stays on the `agenda_document` row + the new
   `FetchRecord.document_outcomes` (durable per-doc provenance).
2. Post-fix re-run (`17-09-53`, image `8bafca6d`): **+14 rows** — every new
   row traced to 12 documents the bounded window slid onto between runs:
   eScribe returns the same meeting *set* in a different order per call, so a
   position-ranked window is unstable. **Fix:** `doc_order_fields` canonical
   ranking (item date desc + id tie-break) — the window is a function of the
   item set.
3. Canonical-order re-run `sig-ingest-escribe-tcv8n` (`17-31-01`, image
   `418f7d4b`): +146 — the one-time transition onto the canonical window.
   **Re-run `sig-ingest-escribe-chgd7` (`17-41-57`): delta 0** — identical
   300-document window (verified: `document_outcomes` URL sets equal,
   outcomes identical 269 no_match / 31 matched), 0 new claim rows.

## Decisions / deviations

- **CivicClerk task timeout.** The bounded window (≤350 docs over ~295 tenant
  indexes) plus sink writes exceeded the 30m ingest-task bound; the shared
  ingest timeout is now 60m in `ops/gcp/scheduled-ops.sh` and the deployed job
  was updated in place. The *window bounds* are unchanged — the run stays
  finite; the ceiling was scheduling, not scope.
- **CivicClerk cloud-egress refusal** is a source-side condition recorded
  honestly — the deterministic path is fixture-proven and a local gated run
  supplies the platform's live document evidence.
- **`contract_notice` flood risk noted:** the contract-family term matches
  most procurement text — it is deliberately part of the reviewed vocab (the
  ticket names `contract_matter_patterns` as in-scope) and rides `value`/`kind`
  as data; per-term selectivity is a vocabulary review concern, not a code one.
- **Claim identity excludes capture id.** `evidence.capture_digest` was
  removed from claim dicts after the first deployed re-run proved eScribe
  pages byte-volatile (+328 duplicate claims). The capture↔document mapping
  moved to the durable side channels (`agenda_document` row →
  `FetchRecord.document_outcomes`) — claims assert "this literal appears in
  the document at this locator", a statement independent of which byte-capture
  established it.
- **Canonical window order.** `doc_order_fields` ranks the bounded window by
  item data (date desc, id tie-break) after the +14 rerun delta traced to
  eScribe's per-call random index ordering. The ticket's "same bounded window"
  is now a function of the item set — proven: runs C/D selected byte-identical
  300-doc windows and added 0 claims.

## Honest limits

- `raw_value` is the matched literal only — never a free-text excerpt — and the
  `byte_range` locator indexes the *extracted* document text (the OKC
  convention), not raw bytes.
- PrimeGov contributes zero document evidence while the platform robots wall
  stands (D-SOURCES.2-4 stays PARTIAL — operator API-mode decision owed).
- CivicClerk's deployed-leg evidence is `access_restricted` at Cloud Run
  egress; whether that settles or is a standing WAF rule is a next-run
  observation.
- `agenda_document` run rows are report/fetch-record artifacts, not spine
  claims (`record_kind != "claim"` is sink-skipped by design); their
  per-document outcomes persist via `FetchRecord.document_outcomes`.
- The **first** post-fix re-runs of legistar/civicclerk will each re-insert
  their document/content claims once (the digest re-baseline — the claim
  identity changed when `capture_digest` left the evidence dict), then dedupe
  from there — same one-time transition eScribe showed (+331, then +146 on the
  canonical-window move, then 0).
- eScribe's server-side ordering instability means a *changed* item set (a
  genuinely added/cancelled meeting) still legitimately shifts the window —
  new claims for genuinely new evidence are correct append-only behavior.
